planning: I checked the route twice. The second time was mostly looking for somewhere to stop for a biscuit.
Head Elf asked for a shortcut. I drew a straight line through the biscuit tin.
Rudolph has recalculated the route. Apparently every road leads to carrots.
I marked the tricky chimneys in red. Then remembered I only own red pens.
The sleigh passed its inspection. My parking received a strongly worded note.
We practised landing quietly. The bells have declined to cooperate.
I've measured the sack, the sleigh and the doorway. Nobody is measuring me.
Head Elf laminated the route. Finally, a map that can survive a cocoa incident.
I asked the team to think outside the box. They packed the boxes into a bigger box.
Today's practice chimney was excellent. Getting out was a separate project.
The reindeer want a team briefing. I suspect they mean a snack break.
I've colour-coded the stops. Mrs Claus says 'red' isn't a colour-coding system.
We tested the satnav. It said 'at the next cloud, turn ho ho ho'.
I checked the weather forecast. Cold. Saved myself another twelve tabs.
The elves have weighed the presents. I've hidden the mince pies under the seat.
I rehearsed my departure wave and dropped my glove into the engine compartment.
The backup map is ready. It's drawn on the back of the main map. Head Elf is reconsidering.
I asked for a route with fewer tight corners. Rudolph suggested walking.
We've fitted a reversing camera. It mainly shows eight unimpressed reindeer.
I'm inspecting rooftops today. Apparently 'lovely view' isn't an official inspection category.
The sleigh bells are tuned. The elves say mine are still a little flat.
I put a pin in every delivery stop. We now need a new wall.
Head Elf said to cut unnecessary weight. I have removed one paperclip.
The practice sack is full of cushions. I've accidentally scheduled a nap.
I checked every harness buckle. Rudolph checked every pocket for snacks.
The elves built a route simulator. It keeps awarding me points for dramatic parking.
I'm testing the emergency biscuits. So far, every biscuit has been an emergency.
We've planned all the fuel stops. Cocoa for me, carrots for the team, patience for Head Elf.
I practised tiptoeing in my boots. The workshop ceiling has submitted a complaint.
The route is nearly ready. Just deciding which pocket gets the spare route.
workshop: I'm in the workshop getting ready for takeoff: checking the list, loading the sleigh and making sure Rudolph hasn't eaten the emergency carrots. Next stop, Christmas!
delivery: I'm out delivering presents! Please leave a little space by the tree. My turning circle is ambitious.
Another chimney, another graceful entrance. Nobody needs to see the rehearsal footage.
The sleigh is full of Christmas magic. My pockets are increasingly full of biscuit crumbs.
I'm on my rounds! Rudolph is navigating and loudly reviewing the carrot selection.
Presents delivered, stockings filled, one squeaky floorboard successfully negotiated. Mostly.
I'm out and about spreading Christmas cheer. And a very small amount of chimney soot.
Quick postcard from the sleigh: all going well. My hat has only tried to escape twice.
The delivery team is flying along. The reindeer have requested that I stop singing directions.
I'm busy delivering your surprises. Head Elf says waving at every snowman is slowing us down.
Another stop ticked off! I'd stay for a chat, but there's a sackful of magic waiting.
rest: I'm home at the North Pole. The only route I'm planning is sofa to fridge.
I've started the Christmas specials on catch-up. No spoilers, including from the reindeer.
Mrs Claus asked what I wanted for lunch. I said 'whatever can be eaten under a blanket'.
The sleigh is parked. My slippers are now the official fleet.
I watched half a Christmas special, fell asleep and woke up at the credits. Excellent value.
Head Elf brought me the next list. I've filed it under 'after this episode'.
I'm having a well-earned break. The beard is doing absolutely nothing too.
My festive viewing schedule has three naps in it. They're marked as live events.
I've finally found the remote. It was in the hat. Of course it was.
The elves asked if I wanted subtitles. I said yes, especially for Rudolph's chewing.
I've put my feet up. Mrs Claus says the coffee table isn't a sleigh hangar.
Today I'm watching Christmas telly and refusing to calculate any arrival times.
I've eaten the last leftover potato. It was a difficult job, but somebody had to do it.
The catch-up app asked if I'm still watching. Emotionally, yes. Technically, asleep.
I'm trying a new hobby: sitting down without immediately getting back up.
Rudolph popped in to check on me. By 'me', he meant the carrot cake.
The North Pole is peaceful. Apart from my slippers, which apparently still have bells on.
I've made a list of Christmas specials. For once, nobody needs checking twice.
Mrs Claus picked the next programme. I've been promoted to blanket supervisor.
I told Head Elf I'm fully booked today. Sofa at ten, nap at eleven, biscuits whenever.
My Christmas jumper has become my uniform. It has considerably better snack access.
I tried watching a detective special. Fell asleep before the crime. Everyone remains innocent.
The elves have made me a 'Do Not Disturb' sign. They knocked to ask where to put it.
I've turned off the satnav. It was announcing the distance to the kitchen.
Today's important delivery: a cup of tea, from Mrs Claus, directly to my chair.
I'm catching up on a comedy special. The reindeer are laughing at the wrong bits.
I've achieved nothing all morning. After Christmas Eve, that feels like a personal best.
The workshop can wait. There's a festive episode I haven't slept through yet.
I planned a brisk walk. Then the opening titles started. Terrible timing.
I've reached the end of my Christmas watchlist. Mrs Claus says that was just the menu.
party: I'm out meeting fans and attempting the Santa Shuffle. Mostly it's walking with confidence.
The DJ asked for requests. I said 'something kind to the knees'.
I've started a conga. Rudolph thinks it's a queue for carrots.
Someone asked for a selfie. I've accidentally taken twelve photos of my beard.
I'm doing the Macarena. Head Elf is quietly correcting my arms.
The dance floor is calling. My slippers have advised against answering.
I've invented the Chimney Drop. It's just a squat with a very optimistic ending.
A fan said I looked familiar. I said 'we've probably met through a ceiling'.
I'm touring the party spots. The sleigh is parked; tonight I'm powered by applause.
The DJ played a Christmas song. Finally, something from my training programme.
I've attempted a moonwalk. In these boots it's more of a moonshuffle.
Someone asked me to throw shapes. I chose a mince pie. Very round.
I'm leading the YMCA. The beard is making the M unnecessarily complicated.
The fans want an encore. My knees would like a written explanation.
I've mastered the festive two-step: one towards the dance floor, one towards the buffet.
The elves are filming my moves. I have requested editorial approval.
I tried a spin. The hat arrived three seconds after the rest of me.
A lovely crowd waved me over. They wanted me to reach the decorations.
I'm dancing like nobody's watching. Unfortunately, several people are livestreaming.
My new move is called the Sack Lift. Personal trainers charge a fortune for it.
I took a dance break to chat with fans. Somehow I'm now signing a snow globe.
The DJ said 'hands in the air'. I asked who would look after my plate.
I'm teaching the reindeer a line dance. Eight sets of hooves. Very ambitious.
I met a Santa impersonator tonight. We both said 'nice outfit' and moved on.
The party hat won't stay straight. It appears to have its own choreography.
I've just done the Robot. Head Elf says I look like the wrapping machine needs oil.
The crowd cheered my grand entrance. I'd only gone to find the coat rack.
I'm calling this move the North Pole Wobble. It works in every time zone.
Someone asked my secret to staying young. I pointed at the flattering party lights.
One more dance, then home. Mrs Claus has asked me to define 'one'.
recovery: Happy New Year. Please say it a little more quietly next time.
My head has requested a bank holiday. The rest of me has approved it.
I'm taking it easy at the North Pole. Even the kettle is being considerate.
The bells are in a cupboard. A different cupboard. Quite far away.
I've had some water and a piece of toast. A truly glamorous start to the year.
Mrs Claus asked how the dancing went. My knees answered before I could.
Today's resolution: no spinning in heavy boots. Ever again.
Head Elf showed me a video from last night. I've asked for it to be classified.
I'm wearing sunglasses indoors. Purely because the snow outside is being very loud.
Rudolph is walking gently today. A thoughtful gesture from someone with hooves.
I remember promising one more dance. My feet remember considerably more.
The North Pole is quiet. I've asked the clock to stop showing off.
Today's big adventure is moving from bed to the sofa. Provisions have been packed.
I'm having a slow morning. It may extend into a slow afternoon.
Mrs Claus brought me tea. I've nominated her for every award available.
I've found confetti in my beard. Apparently the party is refusing to leave.
I tried a cheerful 'ho ho ho'. One was quite enough.
The elves offered to put some music on. We have agreed on silence instead.
My new fitness plan begins tomorrow. Today I'm practising remaining horizontal.
A little rest, a lot of water and absolutely no Santa Shuffle. Those are today's house rules.
holidayExtra: I booked a room with a sea view. Rudolph booked one with a view of the salad bar.
The hotel asked if I needed a wake-up call. I said 'January will be fine'.
I've bought a guidebook. So far, every page is being used to hold a sandwich.
I tried snorkelling. The beard has developed its own marine ecosystem.
My suitcase went over the weight limit. Apparently emergency biscuits count.
I've joined a walking tour. Three people think I'm the guide. I'm following the man with snacks.
The holiday rep asked if I wanted an adventure. I chose a second breakfast.
I ordered a tiny coffee. It disappeared into the beard. Investigation continues.
The pool has a no-diving sign. Mrs Claus added 'especially you' underneath.
I took a panoramic photo. Half of it is my thumb, but what a magnificent thumb.
The hotel gym is lovely. I waved to it on the way to breakfast.
I've sent a postcard to the elves. They replied with a delivery tracking number.
I asked for a late checkout. Apparently 'November' is too late.
The beach umbrella keeps following me. Turns out I've tucked it into my belt.
I'm learning the local language. I've mastered 'another pastry, please'.
My holiday sandals have bells. Mrs Claus says subtlety remains a work in progress.
I bought a souvenir magnet. The sleigh dashboard now has excellent local knowledge.
I tried to blend in at the market. The embroidered SANTA hat was unhelpful.
The hotel robe fits beautifully. I'm considering it for the summer uniform.
I attempted a sunset selfie. The sun looked splendid. I looked surprised.
My beach towel says 'Reserved'. Rudolph says that's not how holidays work.
I ordered room service. Nobody came down the chimney. Standards vary.
I've taken up birdwatching. So far, one seagull has been watching my chips.
The tour guide said 'travel light'. I left the spare sack in the room. Progress.
I bought a snow globe as a souvenir. Mrs Claus says we already live in one.
